blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Built from provincial and municipal pages named under Sources, read November 1, 2026.
These BC rules apply to every land purchase on this site, whichever neighbourhood it is in. They are written once here; each community page covers only what is specific to that community.
GST on vacant land — CRA GI-003 level only

most sales of vacant land by individuals are exempt (land kept for personal use is the CRA's example), while a sale can be taxable where the land is used in a business, sold in the course of a business, or is a parcel created by subdividing another parcel into more than two parts; sales of newly subdivided lots by a developer/business are generally taxable. The live page's GST and down-payment summaries are the page's own summaries and are not adopted here.
Property transfer tax

general 1% on the first $200,000, 2% to $2 million, 3% above $2 million, plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3 million; First-Time Home Buyers' Program (first $500,000 exempt at values of $835,000 or less, maximum saving $8,000, partial $835,000–$860,000); Newly Built Home Exemption (full to $1,100,000, partial to $1,150,000 — a new-HOME exemption, not bare land; a person who paid PTT on vacant land and then has a newly built home on it may be eligible for a refund of the tax paid). Worked examples, inputs + tier math stated (fully residential, no exemption unless stated): $500,000 → $2,000 + $6,000 = $8,000; $700,000 → $2,000 + $10,000 = $12,000; $800,000 → $2,000 + $12,000 = $14,000 (fully-qualifying first-time buyer: $6,000); $900,000 → $16,000; $1,000,000 → $18,000; $1,200,000 → $22,000; $1,500,000 → $2,000 + $26,000 = $28,000; $1,800,000 → $2,000 + $32,000 = $34,000; $2,000,000 → $38,000; $3,500,000 → $2,000 + $36,000 + $45,000 (3% tier) + $10,000 (further 2% on the $500,000 over $3M) = $93,000.
FTHB GST rebate / programs — land angle

the FTHB rebate (Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026 per CRA News No. 122; 100% to $1M, maximum $50,000, phasing to $1.5M; agreements Mar 20, 2025–2031) applies to new HOUSING, not bare land itself. New Housing Rebate 36% / maximum $6,300 / $350,000–$450,000 phase-out. Home Buyers' Plan $60,000; FHSA $40,000 lifetime / $8,000 per year.
GST on vacant land — CRA level only

CRA Info Sheet GI-003 states most sales of vacant land by individuals are exempt (personal-use land), while sales can be taxable where land was used primarily in a business, sold in the course of a business, or created by subdividing into more than two parts; developer/business sales and newly subdivided lots are therefore generally TAXABLE, an individual's personal-use sale generally exempt. The Tsawwassen lots-and-land page's own GST summary was left UNVERIFIED against a CRA source in the topic research and is not restated here. Finer points: UNCONFIRMED per parcel.
Speculation/vacancy + purchase prohibition
no East Cambie-specific position is documented in the research — none imported.
FTHB GST rebate

new HOUSING, not bare land (Bill C-4, assent March 13, 2026; 100% to $1,000,000, maximum $50,000, phasing to $1,500,000; March 20, 2025–2031); its application to a court transaction sits inside the UNCONFIRMED court-sale tax question. New Housing Rebate 36% / maximum $6,300 / $350,000–$450,000; Home Buyers' Plan $60,000; First Home Savings Account $40,000 / $8,000 per year.
Rebates attach to housing, not bare land

FTHB GST rebate (Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026 per CRA News No. 122; 100% of GST to $1M, max $50,000, phasing to $1.5M, agreements Mar 20, 2025–2031) — a qualifying new HOME purchase, not raw land; New Housing Rebate 36% / max $6,300 / $350,000–$450,000 underneath. HBP $60,000; FHSA $40,000 / $8,000 per year. Whether any of these reaches a specific manufactured-home purchase is a program-eligibility question, UNCONFIRMED in this research.
PTT — worked example (inputs + tier math)

on a $900,000 purchase — 1% on the first $200,000 ($2,000) + 2% on $200,000–$900,000 ($14,000) = $16,000. Tiers: 1% to $200,000, 2% to $2,000,000, 3% above, plus a further 2% on the residential portion over $3,000,000. Newly Built Home Exemption (Province): full PTT exemption at fair market value $1,100,000 or less for a qualifying newly built home as a principal residence, partial phasing out to $1,150,000, effective April 1, 2024 — the live page's FAQ statement of these thresholds matches the Province's page; it is a new-HOME exemption, not a bare-land exemption.
PTT on land

general rates are 1% of fair market value up to and including $200,000, 2% of the portion over $200,000 up to and including $2,000,000, and 3% of the portion over $2,000,000, with a further 2% on the residential portion above $3,000,000. First-time buyers: exempt on the first $500,000 at $835,000 or less, partial to $860,000. Newly Built Home Exemption: full to $1,100,000, eliminated at $1,150,000 — new HOME, not bare land.
Subdivision + servicing requirements

subdivision parcel area, shape and dimensions must conform to the zoning bylaw for the parcel's zone, under the Burnaby Subdivision Control and Development Servicing Bylaw (renamed from the Burnaby Subdivision Control Bylaw 1971 by Amendment Bylaw No. 14667, 2024; the City's servicing updates took effect September 30, 2024). Required works and services include highways and lanes, water distribution connected to the City system, sewage collection and drainage collection, built to the City's Engineering Design Criteria Manual standards; the City's Servicing Improvements Guide addresses servicing for developments with four or more primary dwelling units on a residential lot. Confirm the parcel-level requirement with the City's Engineering Department before pricing a split.
Subdivision / servicing

subdivision runs against the zone minimums in Bylaw No. Verified on the City's own Land Development pages in an earlier program batch: the Surrey Subdivision and Development Bylaw, 1986, No. 8830 is the City's subdivision/servicing bylaw, worked through the Engineering Land Development / Servicing Agreement process. Servicing itself is parcel-specific here: the live page points well/septic buyers to the Province's GWELLS well-record system (carried as the page's guidance, UNVERIFIED on a Province source in the research), and one feed parcel is described as municipally serviced — read the services for the parcel, not the sub-area.

faq.q: Will GST apply if I buy a newly subdivided lot from a developer?
faq.a: Generally yes — developer sales and newly subdivided lots are generally taxable under CRA's vacant-land rules, unlike an individual's personal-use resale (CRA GI-003). The FTHB GST rebate does not rescue a bare-lot purchase: it applies to new housing, not bare land.

faq.q: What is the smallest lot I can create here?
faq.a: By zone: RS Large Lot Residential carries a 0.2 ha subdivision minimum; R-3 / R-4 / R-6 carry 1,215 sq m — a subdivision minimum only, which does not apply to development on existing lots. RM-1 townhouse sites: 0.4 ha; RM-2: 3,035 sq m. Confirm the parcel's zone in Bylaw No. 2505, 2011.

faq.q: What tax do I pay on a lot purchase here?
faq.a: GST depends on the seller and the lot's history at the CRA GI-003 level — the live page's GST and lender down-payment positions are UNVERIFIED in the research; confirm with a CPA per transaction.

faq.q: Will GST apply if I buy a vacant lot?
faq.a: Generally yes if the seller is a developer/business or the lot is newly subdivided; generally no for an individual's personal-use resale, per CRA GI-003 — and the FTHB GST rebate applies to new housing, not bare land itself.

faq.q: Will GST apply if I buy a vacant parcel?
faq.a: Generally yes if the seller is a developer/business or the lot is newly subdivided; generally no for an individual's personal-use resale, per CRA GI-003 — and the FTHB GST rebate applies to new housing, not bare land itself.

No public school inside Dollarton is confirmed — the named schools beside the area are Cove Cliff Elementary and Seycove Secondary in Deep Cove and Seymour Heights Elementary to the north-west, and the catchment for any address must be run with SD44 before it is marketed. Do not market Dorothy Lynas French Immersion as the neighbourhood school; it is a choice program at 4000 Inlet Crescent.

faq.q: Will GST apply to a newly subdivided lot bought from a developer?
faq.a: Generally yes at the CRA GI-003 level — developer sales and newly subdivided lots are generally taxable, unlike an individual's personal-use resale. The FTHB GST rebate applies to new housing, not bare land.

The City's utility wording puts established single-family homes on municipal water (2026 charge $652.33) with sewer as a parcel tax — confirm servicing for the specific parcel with the City before writing, and for a redevelopment lot, the Engineering pre-application is where offsite servicing and any cash-in-lieu are set.
